result.title: Beyond the Training Cameras: Coverage-Controlled Probes of Viewing Direction in Frozen Vision Models
result.summary: Vision models are trained on 2D images of a 3D world. Do their hidden features encode the direction from which the camera views a scene, and if so, in what form? We study the relative viewing direction $α$ of two objects in rendered scenes where both object centres stay at fixed pixels while the camera moves, so that perspective, shading and shadows change but the projected layout does not. In eight pretrained models, from diffusion models to self-supervised and image-text encoders, $α$ is encoded in a strikingly simple form: a single two-dimensional plane in the hidden space, shared across scenes, in which the difference between the two objects' features traces $(\cosα, \sinα)$. The plane keeps its orientation when lighting, colours, floors and object shapes change. This encoding is more than a summary of a few visible measurements: readouts fitted on one set of camera paths stay accurate at camera positions outside their range in seven of the eight models, whereas decoders of the measured object and shadow geometry, equally accurate within that range, fail there. In the diffusion transformer PixArt-$α$, the plane forms abruptly at a single block and carries direction information to later blocks, yet editing it changes the objects rather than the generated viewpoint. We also examine how this encoding carries over to scanned real objects.

AI.brief_summary: 研究冻结视觉模型的隐特征是否编码两物体的相对视角方向：在相机移动而投影布局固定的渲染场景中，发现八个预训练模型均以共享的二维平面、按 (cosα, sinα) 形式编码该方向，并检验跨相机路径泛化及 PixArt-α 中该平面的形成与作用。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接关系视觉几何与任务必要信息是否保留在内部状态、以及读出能否外推到训练范围之外，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与表示压缩的基础；但不涉及推理状态生成或答案对 latent 的使用，联系偏表示诊断而非竞争。
